label: One of 12 specific tokens (c,3,x,q,y,v,l,t,e,g,o,a) arriving at the start of the sequence
explanation: Fires on a fixed set of 12 input tokens (c,3,x,q,y,v,l,t,e,g,o,a) when they come at the very start of the sequence. At t=0 the rule is exact on dev: precision 1.0, and every t=0 step with one of these tokens fires (62% of activations, 72% of activation mass). Magnitude depends on the token: c, 3, x and q are strongest; a and o are weakest. Weaker firing at t=1 when the token is in the set and the previous token was not. Residual (about 14% of mass): weak firing at t=2, and in the copy phase of short sequences (mostly L=3-4) when an early in-set token is fed back in. The largest single activations of all are on the copy-phase re-input of the first token at t=L+1 when L=3. Never fires at the delimiter, and almost never on original tokens after position 2.

issues: The t=0 core claim holds on test: an in-set token at t=0 gives precision 1.0, recall 0.62 and mass recall 0.72.

The t=1 rule ('previous token not in the set') is wrong. That clause has only 0.565 precision on test, so about 44% of its t=1 predictions are false positives, and they are systematic. Firing at t=1 depends on the specific previous token, not on whether it is in the set. Measured on dev: precision is 1.0 after k or u, 0.92 after w, 0.84 after b, 0.82 after p and 0.74 after s or z. It is about 0.4-0.5 after d, h, m, n, r, 2 or j, 0.33 after f, 0.16 after 0 or 1, and 0.0 after i. After an in-set token it is about 0, except after t (0.40) and e (0.17).

The copy-phase residual is mischaracterized. The explanation says it fires 'when an early in-set token is fed back in'. In fact, at L=3, recall_idx=1 (t=4) it also fires 53% of the time when the re-input token is NOT in the set (e.g. j, z), and 97.5% when it is. So that position fires largely regardless of which token comes in.

Correct claims: it never fires at the delimiter, and is essentially silent on original tokens at t>=3 (0 of 346k steps). Token ordering by magnitude (c, 3, x, q strongest; a, o weakest by mass share) matches the profile.
skeptic.revised_label: First token of the sequence is one of c,3,x,q,y,v,l,t,e,g,o,a (exact at t=0). Weaker at t=1 when such a token follows a specific first token (k,u,w,b,p,s,z strongly; d,h,m,n,r,2 partly; never i,0,1 or most in-set tokens). Also fires on the first copy-phase re-input when L=3.
